paragraphs.text: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in COL9A3, which encodes the alpha-3 chain of heterotrimeric type IX collagen. Rad et al. (2022) noted that the consistent features in these patients were moderate to profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss and moderate to high myopia with vitreoretinal degeneration. Retinal detachment and cataract occurred occasionally, and skeletal involvement, including spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, appeared more variable. Markova et al. (2021) noted that none of the patients they reviewed had cleft palate.

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) reported a boy of Indian ancestry, born to consanguineous parents, who was last described at 12 years of age. He failed his newborn hearing screen and had moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss, with mild enlargement of the vestibular aqueducts. He had progressive high myopia, but no vitreous abnormalities or retinal degeneration. Femoral and tibial bowing were present at birth. Radiographs showed slightly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses, flattening of the acetabula, irregular medial distal femoral epiphyses, and mild platyspondyly with irregular vertebral endplates. He had midfacial hypoplasia but no cleft palate or pes planus. Growth, intelligence, and gross motor development were normal, but speech was delayed. He also had autoimmune hypothyroidism.

paragraphs.text: Markova et al. (2021) reported a 3-year-old boy born to nonconsanguineous parents. He had fetal growth retardation and congenital bilateral high myopia. At 11 months of age he was diagnosed with grade 3-4 bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and was fitted with hearing aids. Speech development was delayed. He had hip dysplasia with adductor spasm and limited hip abduction. Radiographs showed spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, which included mild platyspondyly, kyphosis with its apex at T11, spina bifida occulta of the sacral vertebrae, flattened irregular femoral heads, broadened and shortened femoral necks, coxa valga, and flattened distal femoral epiphyses. Eye examination showed peripheral retinal pigment rearrangement with whitish dystrophic foci, multiple vitreous floaters, a preretinal membrane, and vitreoretinal degeneration. The electroretinogram was normal and there was no retinal detachment. Facial features included a flattened nasal bridge, small nose, mild midface hypoplasia, and high palate, without cleft palate. He also had lumbar lordosis, long fingers, deformed prominent knee joints, genu valgum, planovalgus feet, a waddling gait, lower limb joint pain, and rapid fatigability. Markova et al. (2021) compared their patient with 6 previously reported patients from 3 families with COL9A3-related recessive Stickler syndrome. Congenital high myopia and moderately severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss from a very early age were present in all of them, and none had cleft palate.

paragraphs.text: Rad et al. (2022) reported 5 patients from 3 unrelated consanguineous Iranian families. In family 1, the affected individual was a 28-year-old woman, the oldest and only affected of 3 children of first-cousin parents. She had high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with empty vitreous, multiple lattice degenerations, retinal pigmentary changes, and severe progressive sensorineural hearing loss. A skull x-ray showed unilateral absence of the frontal sinus. She also had knee joint pain, short metacarpals with widened epiphyses, an irregular radial epiphysis, mild thoracic platyspondyly, genu valgum, and pes planus. She did not have midface hypoplasia, cleft palate, micrognathia, short stature, or intellectual disability.

paragraphs.text: In family 3 reported by Rad et al. (2022), 2 of 4 children of first-cousin parents were affected: a boy aged 11.8 years and his sister aged 3.1 years. Both also had pes planus, depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nares, midface hypoplasia, and downslanting palpebral fissures, and the last 2 features were more pronounced in the sister. The boy complained of knee joint pain, especially when running. He also had bowed tibiae, genu valgum, short metacarpals, broad big toes, irregular femoral epiphyses, a flat and irregular acetabular roof, flattened femoral heads, and broadened and shortened femoral necks.
